assessments.reasoning: The authors explain machine-suffixed names as names of particular implementations, expressly distinguishing them from their language. They give APL/1130 and APL/360 as examples.

challenge.method: Compare their naming paragraph with the archival IBM cover and acknowledgement, and with Dyalog's description of its own APL-based scope.
challenge.results: The historical passage supports the general APL language referent. Product labels and vendor extensions have separate source boundaries.

limitations: The historical language referent has separate scope from IBM products and later vendor variants.
